newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein firm, CPO up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein firm, CPO up in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were steady in late trading on Tuesday while crude palm oil was traded higher, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,440-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening. Crude palm oil was done at 1,252.50 rupiah/kg at a 500-tonne tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan on Tuesday.

"Crude palm oil is edging up after palm olein prices increased sharply on Monday," one trader said. "But demand in Jakarta was slow after some active buying the past few days. Buyers seem to be taking a breather."
The traders said export prices were still at a premium to local values, adding that players preferred to sell abroad rather than channel their oil to the local market.
"But if local prices continue to rise and overtake export prices, we will see players selling more oil locally," one trader said. "But I don't see this happening yet."

The traders also said they were not surprised by news that the state-run Joint Marketing Board (KPB) had delayed export shipments of about 20,000 tonnes of crude palm oil to June from May because of a decline in production.
"The shipments have been delayed to June from May because of a drop in production," a KPB official told Reuters, adding that the volume was 30-50 percent of its total monthly exports.
The official said he had no details on the production shortfall, but added that the agency's crude palm oil allocation to local refiners was not affected.
"It could be that the situation arose because of KPB's large export commitments coupled with a drop in production," one trader said. "Local allocations are also delayed sometimes."
